sam.k: hey team — first week, trying to build the inference runtime from source on my dev machine (Ubuntu 22.04, WSL2). Followed the devex build doc but getting a bunch of CUDA/compile errors. anyone free to help? :wave:

lina: welcome! can you paste the full error and your nvidia-smi + gcc versions? also are you on a laptop GPU or using a remote GPU node?

sam.k: thanks. i'm on a company loaner (RTX 4090) but running via WSL2, GPU passthrough is enabled. here's the main error i see during cmake/make:

```
-- Found CUDA: /usr/local/cuda (found version "12.2")
[ 12%] Building NVRTC kernel...
/opt/cuda/include/nvrtc.h: No such file or directory
CMake Error at cuda_check.cmake:45 (message):
  CUDA_INCLUDE_DIRS not found or invalid
ld: cannot find -lcuda
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

and `nvidia-smi` shows:

```
Tue Apr 20 12:34:56 2024
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.54.03    Driver Version: 535.54.03    CUDA Version: 12.2     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

`gcc --version` -> `gcc (Ubuntu 11.4.0-1ubuntu1) 11.4.0`

ben: a few things to check: 1) WSL/driver integration can be flaky for native dev builds — recommend using our GPU dev container on a linux VM if possible. 2) Make sure CUDA toolkit and driver match (looks ok: driver 535 + cuda 12.2). 3) Check LD_LIBRARY_PATH and CUDA_HOME. 4) Some build steps expect the toolkit to be at /usr/local/cuda-12.2 or /usr/local/cuda.

lina: also, the "ld: cannot find -lcuda" usually means the linker can't find libcuda.so. run:

```bash
ls -l /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcuda.so* || ls -l /usr/lib/wsl/lib/libcuda.so*
echo $CUDA_HOME $LD_LIBRARY_PATH
```

And try exporting if empty:

```bash
export CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-12.2
export PATH=$CUDA_HOME/bin:$PATH
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$CUDA_HOME/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
```

Then `rm -rf build && mkdir build && cd build && cmake .. && make -j$(nproc)`

sam.k: ran the ls, got nothing under /usr/local/cuda/lib64, but there is a weird symlink under /usr/lib/wsl/lib/libcuda.so -> /proc/driver/nvidia/xxx. PATH/LD_LIBRARY_PATH were empty. set the vars and re-ran cmake, now error changed to:

```
-- Performing Test HAVE_CXX_17 - Success
-- Found CUDA: /usr/local/cuda-12.2 (found version "12.2")
[ 35%] Building third_party/libkernels
In file included from /usr/local/cuda/include/cuda_runtime.h:...
/opt/cuda/include/host_config.h:56:10: fatal error: cuda_runtime_api.h: No such file or directory
56 | #include <cuda_runtime_api.h>
   |          ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
```

ben: that looks like include paths are pointed at /opt/cuda but your toolkit is at /usr/local/cuda-12.2. Are there old leftovers from a previous install. run `sudo update-alternatives --list cuda` and check for stray /opt/cuda links. If using WSL, sometimes the distro has a packaged cuda that conflicts.

lina: if the headers are missing, install the CUDA toolkit (not just driver). In WSL the recommended route is the deb package from NVIDIA: https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-downloads — choose Ubuntu 22.04 WSL2 and CUDA 12.2. Or use our prebuilt dev container image: `ghcr.io/redwood-inference/dev-container:cuda-12.2` which has everything set.

infra: if you want, I can provision a short-lived linux VM with the correct driver/toolkit already installed (non-WSL) — ping me here or open an infra ticket. We also have a GPU sandbox with docker + containerd that works reliably. @sam.k do you want that?

sam.k: yes please @infra, that would save time. one more question — the build doc mentions using `gcc-11` vs system `gcc`. do i need to change compilers?

lina: runtime code needs GCC 11 or 12 ABI. your gcc 11.4 is fine. if you ever hit "unsupported compiler" from nvcc, set cmake to use gcc-11 explicitly:

```bash
cmake .. -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=/usr/bin/gcc-11 -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/usr/bin/g++-11 -DCUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR=/usr/local/cuda-12.2
```

ben: extra tip: if you see weird runtime type errors at link time, try `ldconfig` after installing the toolkit or create /etc/ld.so.conf.d/cuda.conf with `/usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64` then `sudo ldconfig`.

sam.k: awesome — opened an infra ticket (INV-2243) and accepted the VM offer. i'll try the dev-container in meantime. thanks both! :tada:

deploy-bot: CI job rtx-build-12.2 restarted by @lina — seeing similar failures in the Linux/WSL matrix. logs: https://ci.redwood.dev/rtx-build-12.2/5678

lina: marking this thread with onboarding label and adding to the devex doc checklist: add WSL caveat + recommend container/VM for GPU builds.

sam.k: super helpful — feeling less blocked. i'll update here once it's green.

ben: ping if the infra VM shows any missing kernel modules — sometimes the driver needs a reboot on the host (infra will handle).

sam.k: thanks — will do.
